handbook-foundations_caution-data-collec: Caution: Data collection raises privacy, consent, and equity concerns. GDPR and institutional policies must govern all educational data practices.
handbook-foundations_caution-ml-models-r: Caution: ML models reflect biases present in training data. Outcomes may not generalise to populations underrepresented in the data.

handbook-foundations_is-a-broad-field-of: Is: A broad field of computer science focused on creating systems that simulate human cognitive functions such as reasoning, learning, and problem-solving.
handbook-foundations_is-a-subset-of-ai-f: Is: A subset of AI focused on enabling computers to understand, interpret, and generate human language — including text and speech.
handbook-foundations_is-a-subset-of-ai-i: Is: A subset of AI in which algorithms learn patterns from data and improve performance with experience, without being explicitly programmed for each task.
handbook-foundations_is-a-subset-of-ai-t: Is: A subset of AI that enables machines to interpret and analyse visual information — images, videos, and diagrams.
handbook-foundations_is-ai-systems-that-: Is: AI systems that create new content — text, images, audio, code — based on patterns learned from existing data, typically using large language models or diffusion models.
handbook-foundations_is-not-a-cognitive-: Is not: A cognitive technology. Automation executes predefined or learned procedures; it does not reason about educational purpose.
handbook-foundations_is-not-a-reliable-s: Is not: A reliable source of factual information. Generative AI can produce plausible-sounding but incorrect content (hallucinations).
handbook-foundations_is-not-a-rule-based: Is not: A rule-based system. ML does not follow fixed instructions; it infers patterns from examples.
handbook-foundations_is-not-a-single-alg: Is not: A single algorithm or a sentient system. AI is an umbrella term covering many approaches.
handbook-foundations_is-not-a-technology: Is not: A technology itself. Data is a resource that requires ethical collection, storage, and use.
handbook-foundations_is-not-human-level-: Is not: Human-level visual reasoning. CV systems excel at pattern recognition within trained categories but fail on out-of-distribution inputs.
handbook-foundations_is-not-perfect-lang: Is not: Perfect language understanding. NLP systems process patterns statistically; they do not "comprehend" meaning as humans do.
handbook-foundations_is-the-raw-material: Is: The raw material that powers AI systems — learner interactions, assessment results, behavioural patterns, and demographic information collected and processed to train or inform models.
handbook-foundations_is-the-use-of-techn: Is: The use of technology to perform repetitive tasks with minimal human intervention — a capability enabled by AI but not equivalent to it.

handbookMain.ch1Desc: Establishes the conceptual vocabulary educators need before evaluating any AI tool. handbookMain.ch5Desc: Explores AI as a creative partner across four domains: image generation, music composition, 3D design, and science-art fusion. handbookMain.introDesc1: This handbook addresses a fundamental challenge facing educators today: AI is being deployed in schools faster than educators can evaluate it. Our approach is deliberate  we prioritise understanding over adoption, critical thinking over enthusiasm, and pedagogical alignment over technological novelty.

index.projectDesc1: The project "SMART TRANSFORMATION IN EDUCATION WITH ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE" (Smart edu AI) is a Small-scale partnership in school education (KA210-SCH) under the Erasmus+ Programme. It has a duration of 24 months, starting on January 1, 2025, and ending on December 31, 2026, with a total lump sum budget of €60,000
index.smart_edu_desc1: The project titled "SMART TRANSFORMATION IN EDUCATION WITH ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE" (Smart edu AI) will run for 24 months from January 1, 2025, to December 31, 2026. Its main goal is to support personalized learning and development by integrating artificial intelligence (AI) technologies into education. The project focuses on developing student-centered AI applications, training teachers in AI tools, and ensuring equal educational opportunities. It also emphasizes individual learning analysis, data analytics, and sustainable environment skills.
index.smart_edu_desc2: Aligned with Erasmus+ priorities, the project addresses digital transformation, environmental sustainability, climate action, and teacher support. Key themes include AI and data use, ecological skills, inclusion, equality, and non-discrimination.Target groups include students across primary, secondary, and high school levels, especially disadvantaged learners, students with special needs, language barriers, and gifted students. Teachers, educational institutions, administrators, and policymakers are also involved.
index.smart_edu_desc3: Key activities involve AI-assisted training and workshops for teachers and students, carbon footprint reduction and sustainability workshops, AI applications in digital design and music practice, AI-supported teaching for disadvantaged students, augmented reality and simulation science experiments, and feedback sessions. Four main activities are led by partners in France, Spain, Turkey, and Poland.
index.smart_edu_desc4: Expected outcomes include enhanced student learning experiences and academic performance, improved digital literacy for teachers, a data repository, innovative teaching methods, and increased environmental awareness. AI integration will personalize education, improve efficiency, and reduce teachers' workload.
index.smart_edu_desc5: The coordinating organization is Eurolab for Teachers (Poland), with partner organizations France Culture Connection (France), Düzce Milli Egemenlik Bilim ve Sanat Merkezi (Turkey), and Centro Público Integrado O Cruce (Spain).
